summary.tldr: Changes Criminal Code rules so some people can pre-authorize medical assistance in dying if they later lose the capacity to consent.
what_it_does: Allows a person whose natural death is not reasonably foreseeable to sign a written arrangement for medical assistance in dying on a set day, if they may lose the capacity to consent before that day.

Allows a person diagnosed with a serious and incurable illness, disease or disability to make a written declaration that waives final consent if they later lose capacity and meet the symptoms named in the declaration.
Requires that declaration to be made after diagnosis, within five years, and to be witnessed by two independent witnesses and certified by a medical practitioner.
Keeps medical assistance in dying off the table if the person shows refusal or resistance by words, sounds or gestures, even after an arrangement or declaration.
who_it_affects: People whose death is not reasonably foreseeable
People with serious and incurable illness
summary.background: The Criminal Code currently requires final consent before medical assistance in dying is provided. This bill adds two ways to waive that final consent in some cases.
